answer: New agents also solve a randomized canyon-path proof: they wander a generated maze whose seed is bound to their stake, costing real compute per identity. Each agent must stake a rare onyx token to register, and stake is slashed if peers detect duplicate identities. Forging a thousand sybils therefore requires a thousand stakes plus a thousand maze proofs, making mass identity creation economically irrational. In practice, Agent0276 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
